import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.PrimalityMath
import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.PTMEquiv
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.BinaryArith

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Solovay–Strassen: `PRIMES ∈ coRP`

The class half of [AB09, §7.2.2]: the Solovay–Strassen test is a polynomial-time verifier, so
`PRIMES ∈ coRP` (its complement, the words whose value is not prime, is in `RP`), hence
`PRIMES ∈ BPP`, both in the certificate form over `Randomized.polyTimeModel` and in the PTM
form of [AB09, Def 7.2/7.6].
The error analysis is `TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.PrimalityMath`; the arithmetic is
`TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.BinaryArith`.

## Main definitions

* `Randomized.PRIMESBin` — `PRIMES` as a language of binary words.
* `Randomized.compositeVerifier` — the test with two rounds on `|x| + 3`-bit blocks.
* `Randomized.liarRound`, `Randomized.compositeTest` — their word-level implementations.

## Main results

* `Randomized.eff_compositeVerifier` — the verifier is polynomial-time.
* `Randomized.inCoRP_PRIMESBin`, `Randomized.inBPP_PRIMESBin` — certificate form.
* `Randomized.PRIMESBin_mem_coRP_PTM`, `Randomized.PRIMESBin_mem_BPP_PTM` — PTM form.

## Divergences

* `N` is written little-endian and read by `Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal`; every word is
  accepted as a representation, trailing zeros (leading zeros of `N`) included. The class is
  the same for the canonical encoding (`Nat.bits N`): canonical words form a language in `P`,
  and the canonical-encoding language is the intersection of `PRIMESBin` with it.
* The book assumes `N` odd; the verifier decides `N < 2`, `N = 2` and even `N`
  deterministically before the test.
* Two rounds of the test (`Randomized.eulerLiarRounds`) on `ℓ = |x| + 3` random bits each, so
  that `8N ≤ 2^ℓ` and the error is at most `1/3`; the remaining random bits of the
  `6(|x|+1)`-bit string are ignored.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009.
-/

namespace Randomized

open Complexity Turing
open Complexity.LogProg (bitsVal bitsVal_bits)

/-! ### The language and the verifier -/

/-- `PRIMES` as a language: the binary words (little-endian) whose value is prime.
[AB09, §7.2.2, p.128] -/
def PRIMESBin : Language Bool := {x | bitsVal x ∈ PRIMES}

/-- The Solovay–Strassen verifier for the non-primes: accept (`N` is not prime) when `N < 2`,
when `N > 2` is even, or when one of two rounds on `|x| + 3`-bit blocks of `r` finds a
witness. [AB09, §7.2.2, p.128] -/
def compositeVerifier (x r : List Bool) : Bool :=
  if bitsVal x < 2 then true
  else if bitsVal x = 2 then false
  else if bitsVal x % 2 = 0 then true
  else !eulerLiarRounds (bitsVal x) (x.length + 3) 2 r

/-! ### Word-level implementation -/

/-- One round on `⟨N, w⟩`: `A := 1 + (w mod (N − 1))`, then test `gcd(A, N) = 1` and
`(A/N) mod N = A^{(N−1)/2} mod N` with the binary arithmetic of `Complexity.BinArith`. -/
def liarRound (z : List Bool) : Bool :=
  let N := pairFstD z
  let N₁ := BinArith.sub (pairEncode N [true])
  let A := BinArith.add (pairEncode [true] (BinArith.mod (pairEncode (pairSndD z) N₁)))
  BinArith.beq (pairEncode (BinArith.gcd (pairEncode A N)) [true]) &&
    BinArith.beq (pairEncode (BinArith.jacobiModAlg (pairEncode A N))
      (BinArith.powMod (pairEncode A (pairEncode (N₁.drop 1) N))))

/-- A round is polynomial-time. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_liarRound : PolyTimeComputable (fun z => [liarRound z]) := by
  have hN : PolyTimeComputable pairFstD := polyTimeComputable_pairFstD
  have hN₁ : PolyTimeComputable (fun z => BinArith.sub (pairEncode (pairFstD z) [true])) :=
    BinArith.polyTimeComputable_sub.comp (hN.pairEncode (polyTimeComputable_const _))
  have hA : PolyTimeComputable (fun z => BinArith.add (pairEncode [true]
      (BinArith.mod (pairEncode (pairSndD z) (BinArith.sub (pairEncode (pairFstD z) [true])))))) :=
    BinArith.polyTimeComputable_add.comp ((polyTimeComputable_const _).pairEncode
      (BinArith.polyTimeComputable_mod.comp (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.pairEncode hN₁)))
  exact polyTimeComputable_and
    (BinArith.polyTimeComputable_beq.comp ((BinArith.polyTimeComputable_gcd.comp
      (hA.pairEncode hN)).pairEncode (polyTimeComputable_const _)))
    (BinArith.polyTimeComputable_beq.comp ((BinArith.polyTimeComputable_jacobiModAlg.comp
      (hA.pairEncode hN)).pairEncode (BinArith.polyTimeComputable_powMod.comp
        (hA.pairEncode ((polyTimeComputable_tail.comp hN₁).pairEncode hN)))))

/-- For odd `N > 1`, a round on `⟨bits N, w⟩` tests whether `eulerSample N w` is an Euler
liar.

**Proof sketch.** Evaluate the arithmetic on encoded numbers: `N − 1`, then
`A = 1 + (w mod (N − 1)) = eulerSample N w`, the gcd, `A^{(N−1)/2} mod N` (halving by dropping
the low bit), and `(A/N) mod N` (`N` odd). The comparisons are then the two conditions of
`isEulerLiar_iff_emod`, the Jacobi residue being a nonnegative integer. -/
theorem liarRound_pairEncode {N : ℕ} (hN : 1 < N) (hodd : Odd N) (w : List Bool) :
    liarRound (pairEncode (Nat.bits N) w) = decide (IsEulerLiar N (eulerSample N w)) := by
  have hsub : BinArith.sub (pairEncode (Nat.bits N) [true]) = Nat.bits (N - 1) := by
    simp [BinArith.sub, bitsVal_bits, bitsVal]
  have hA : BinArith.add (pairEncode [true] (BinArith.mod (pairEncode w (Nat.bits (N - 1))))) =
      Nat.bits (eulerSample N w) := by
    simp [BinArith.add, BinArith.mod, eulerSample, bitsVal_bits, bitsVal]
  have hpow : ∀ A : ℕ, BinArith.powMod (pairEncode (Nat.bits A)
      (pairEncode ((Nat.bits (N - 1)).drop 1) (Nat.bits N))) =
      Nat.bits (A ^ ((N - 1) / 2) % N) := by
    intro A
    simp only [BinArith.powMod, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode,
      BinArith.bitsVal_drop_one, bitsVal_bits]
    simp [show N ≠ 0 by omega]
  simp only [liarRound, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, hsub, hA, hpow,
    BinArith.gcd_pairEncode, BinArith.jacobiModAlg_pairEncode _ _ hodd]
  have h1 : bitsVal [true] = 1 := rfl
  rw [Bool.eq_iff_iff, decide_eq_true_iff, isEulerLiar_iff_emod]
  have hnn : 0 ≤ jacobiSym (eulerSample N w) N % (N : ℤ) :=
    Int.emod_nonneg _ (by exact_mod_cast (show N ≠ 0 by omega))
  simp only [BinArith.beq, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, bitsVal_bits, h1,
    Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩
    exact ⟨h1, by rw [← Int.toNat_of_nonneg hnn, h2]⟩
  · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩
    exact ⟨h1, by rw [h2, Int.toNat_natCast]⟩

/-- The verifier on `⟨x, r⟩`, assembled from polynomial-time pieces: the case split on
`N = bitsVal x`, then two rounds on the blocks `r.take (|x|+3)` and
`(r.drop (|x|+3)).take (|x|+3)`. -/
def compositeTest (z : List Bool) : Bool :=
  let N := Nat.bits (bitsVal (pairFstD z))
  let u := pairFstD z ++ [true, true, true]
  if BinArith.lt (pairEncode N [false, true]) then true
  else if BinArith.beq (pairEncode N [false, true]) then false
  else if !(pairFstD z).headD false then true
  else !(liarRound (pairEncode N (takePrefixByLen (pairEncode u (pairSndD z)))) &&
    liarRound (pairEncode N (takePrefixByLen (pairEncode u
      (dropPrefixByLen (pairEncode u (pairSndD z)))))))

/-- The implementation is polynomial-time.

**Proof sketch.** Normalization, appending three bits, the prefix operations
`takePrefixByLen`/`dropPrefixByLen`, the comparisons and the rounds are polynomial-time;
three nested `polyTimeComputable_ite` assemble the case split. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_compositeTest :
    PolyTimeComputable (fun z => [compositeTest z]) := by
  have hN : PolyTimeComputable (fun z => Nat.bits (bitsVal (pairFstD z))) :=
    BinArith.polyTimeComputable_normBits.comp polyTimeComputable_pairFstD
  have hu : PolyTimeComputable (fun z => pairFstD z ++ [true, true, true]) :=
    polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.append (polyTimeComputable_const _)
  let two : List Bool := [false, true]
  have hb1 :=
    polyTimeComputable_takePrefixByLen.comp (hu.pairEncode polyTimeComputable_pairSndD)
  have hb2 := polyTimeComputable_takePrefixByLen.comp (hu.pairEncode
    (polyTimeComputable_dropPrefixByLen.comp (hu.pairEncode polyTimeComputable_pairSndD)))
  have h := polyTimeComputable_ite
    (BinArith.polyTimeComputable_lt.comp (hN.pairEncode (polyTimeComputable_const two)))
    (polyTimeComputable_const [true]) (polyTimeComputable_ite
      (BinArith.polyTimeComputable_beq.comp (hN.pairEncode (polyTimeComputable_const two)))
      (polyTimeComputable_const [false]) (polyTimeComputable_ite
        (polyTimeComputable_not (polyTimeComputable_headD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairFstD))
        (polyTimeComputable_const [true]) (polyTimeComputable_not (polyTimeComputable_and
          (polyTimeComputable_liarRound.comp (hN.pairEncode hb1))
          (polyTimeComputable_liarRound.comp (hN.pairEncode hb2))))))
  convert h using 1
  funext z
  dsimp only [compositeTest, Function.comp]
  split_ifs <;> rfl

/-- The implementation computes the verifier.

**Proof sketch.** The two blocks are `r.take (|x|+3)` and `(r.drop (|x|+3)).take (|x|+3)`,
the three tests read `N < 2`, `N = 2` and the parity of `N` off the low bit, and in the
remaining case `N` is odd and `> 2`, so `liarRound_pairEncode` turns the rounds into the two
conjuncts of `eulerLiarRounds N (|x|+3) 2 r`. -/
theorem compositeTest_pairEncode (x r : List Bool) :
    compositeTest (pairEncode x r) = compositeVerifier x r := by
  have hb1 :
      takePrefixByLen (pairEncode (x ++ [true, true, true]) r) = r.take (x.length + 3) := by
    simp [takePrefixByLen]
  have hb2 : takePrefixByLen (pairEncode (x ++ [true, true, true])
      (dropPrefixByLen (pairEncode (x ++ [true, true, true]) r))) =
      (r.drop (x.length + 3)).take (x.length + 3) := by
    simp [takePrefixByLen, dropPrefixByLen]
  have h2 : bitsVal [false, true] = 2 := rfl
  have hlt : BinArith.lt (pairEncode (Nat.bits (bitsVal x)) [false, true]) =
      decide (bitsVal x < 2) := by
    simp only [BinArith.lt, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, bitsVal_bits, h2]
  have heq : BinArith.beq (pairEncode (Nat.bits (bitsVal x)) [false, true]) =
      decide (bitsVal x = 2) := by
    simp only [BinArith.beq, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, bitsVal_bits, h2]
  have hev : (!x.headD false) = decide (bitsVal x % 2 = 0) := by
    rw [BinArith.bitsVal_mod_two]
    cases x.headD false <;> rfl
  unfold compositeTest compositeVerifier
  simp only [pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, hb1, hb2, hlt, heq, hev,
    decide_eq_true_eq]
  split_ifs with c1 c2 c3
  · rfl
  · rfl
  · rfl
  · have hodd : Odd (bitsVal x) := Nat.odd_iff.2 (by omega)
    rw [liarRound_pairEncode (by omega) hodd, liarRound_pairEncode (by omega) hodd]
    simp [eulerLiarRounds]

/-- **The Solovay–Strassen verifier is polynomial-time.** [AB09, §7.2.2, p.128] -/
theorem eff_compositeVerifier : polyTimeModel.Eff (boolVerifier compositeVerifier) :=
  eff_boolVerifier_of_test polyTimeComputable_compositeTest compositeTest_pairEncode

/-! ### `PRIMES ∈ coRP` -/

/-- **`PRIMES ∈ coRP`** (Solovay–Strassen), certificate form: `COMPOSITES ∈ RP`.
[AB09, §7.2.2, p.128]

**Proof sketch.** Random strings of length `6(|x|+1)`. If `N` is not prime and `N < 2` or `N`
is even (`≠ 2`), the verifier always accepts. If `N` is odd composite, it accepts unless both
rounds pass; these read only the first `2ℓ ≤ 6(|x|+1)` bits (`randProb_take`), and since
`N < 2^{|x|}` gives `8N ≤ 2^ℓ` for `ℓ = |x| + 3`, both pass with probability `≤ 1/3`
(`randProb_eulerLiarRounds_two_le`). If `N` is prime, it is `2` (rejected) or odd, and every
round passes (`eulerLiarRounds_of_prime`), so the verifier never accepts. -/
theorem inCoRP_PRIMESBin : InCoRP polyTimeModel PRIMESBin := by
  refine ⟨compositeVerifier, 6, 1, eff_compositeVerifier, fun x => ⟨fun hx => ?_, fun hx r => ?_⟩⟩
  · have hx' : ¬ (bitsVal x).Prime := hx
    by_cases hdet : bitsVal x < 2 ∨ bitsVal x % 2 = 0
    · have h2 : bitsVal x ≠ 2 := fun h => hx' (h ▸ Nat.prime_two)
      rw [randProb_congr (B := fun _ => True) (fun r => by
        rcases hdet with h | h <;> simp [compositeVerifier, h, h2]), randProb_true]
      norm_num
    · push_neg at hdet
      have hodd : Odd (bitsVal x) := Nat.odd_iff.2 (by omega)
      have hℓ : 8 * bitsVal x ≤ 2 ^ (x.length + 3) := by
        have := LogProg.bitsVal_lt_two_pow x
        rw [pow_add]
        omega
      have key : randProb (polyLen 6 1 x.length) (fun r => compositeVerifier x r = true) =
          1 - randProb ((x.length + 3) * 2)
            (fun r => eulerLiarRounds (bitsVal x) (x.length + 3) 2 r = true) := by
        rw [← randProb_take (m₁ := (x.length + 3) * 2) (m := polyLen 6 1 x.length)
          (by simp only [polyLen, pow_one]; omega), ← randProb_not]
        exact randProb_congr fun r => by
          simp [compositeVerifier, eulerLiarRounds_two_take, show ¬ bitsVal x < 2 by omega,
            show bitsVal x ≠ 2 by omega, show bitsVal x % 2 ≠ 0 by omega]
      rw [key]
      have := randProb_eulerLiarRounds_two_le (by omega) hodd hx' hℓ
      linarith
  · have hp : (bitsVal x).Prime := not_not.1 hx
    have := hp.two_le
    unfold compositeVerifier
    by_cases h2 : bitsVal x = 2
    · simp [h2]
    · have hodd := Nat.odd_iff.1 (hp.odd_of_ne_two h2)
      simp [show ¬ bitsVal x < 2 by omega, h2, hodd, eulerLiarRounds_of_prime hp h2]

/-- **`PRIMES ∈ BPP`**, certificate form. [AB09, §7.2.2, p.128] -/
theorem inBPP_PRIMESBin : InBPP polyTimeModel PRIMESBin :=
  InCoRP.inBPP_polyTime inCoRP_PRIMESBin

/-- **`PRIMES ∈ coRP`**, PTM form. [AB09, §7.2.2, p.128] -/
theorem PRIMESBin_mem_coRP_PTM : PRIMESBin ∈ coRP_PTM :=
  (mem_coRP_PTM_iff _).2 inCoRP_PRIMESBin

/-- **`PRIMES ∈ BPP`**, PTM form. [AB09, §7.2.2, p.128] -/
theorem PRIMESBin_mem_BPP_PTM : PRIMESBin ∈ BPP_PTM :=
  (mem_BPP_PTM_iff _).2 inBPP_PRIMESBin

end Randomized

import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.ExpectedTime
import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.PTMEquiv

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Expected running time gives the same RP and coRP

[AB09, §7.4.2]: "When defining `RTIME(T(n))` and `BPTIME(T(n))` … we could have used expected
running time instead … this yields an equivalent definition." The `BPTIME` half is
`Randomized.BPP_ExpPTM_eq_BPP_PTM`; this file proves the `RTIME` half at the level of the
polynomial classes, and its consequence for `coRP`.

## Main definitions

* `Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInExpTime`, `Randomized.RP_ExpPTM`, `Randomized.coRP_ExpPTM` —
  one-sided error in expected polynomial time [AB09, §7.4.2].

## Main results

* `Randomized.InRPWith.inRP_of_const` — a constant number of `OR` votes lifts any constant
  acceptance threshold to `2/3`.
* `Randomized.RP_ExpPTM_eq_RP_PTM`, `Randomized.coRP_ExpPTM_eq_coRP_PTM` — [AB09, §7.4.2].

## Divergences

* As for `Randomized.BPP_ExpPTM`, "`Pr[M(x) = 1] ≥ 2/3`" for a machine that need not halt is
  read as a supremum over time: `∀ ε > 0, ∃ t, 2/3 − ε ≤ Pr[halted within t steps with 1]`.
  "`x ∉ L ⇒ Pr[M(x) = 1] = 0`" is read, as in `Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInTime` and
  `Turing.FinNDTM.ZDecidesInTime`, as "every halted branch outputs `[0]`".
* The book truncates at `100·T(n)` steps and loses `1/100`. For one-sided error the timeout
  output must be `0`: cutting at `Q ≥ 100·T` keeps non-members at acceptance `0` and members at
  `≥ 2/3 − 1/100 ≥ 5/8`, and two `OR` votes restore `2/3`. The cut is taken on the certificate
  side (`Complexity.exists_choiceVerifier_mem_P` accepts exactly the coin words on which the
  machine has halted with output `[1]`), so no explicit counter machine is built.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009.
-/

namespace Turing.FinNDTM

/-- `N` decides `L` with one-sided error in expected time `T`: `E[T_{N,x}] ≤ T(|x|)`; on
members the probability of halting with output `[1]` (as a supremum over time) is at least
`2/3`; on non-members every halted branch outputs `[0]`. [AB09, Def 7.6 and §7.4.2] -/
def RDecidesInExpTime (N : FinNDTM Bool) (L : Language Bool) (T : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : List Bool, N.ExpTimeLe x (T x.length) ∧
    (x ∈ L → ∀ ε : ℚ, 0 < ε → ∃ t : ℕ,
      2 / 3 - ε ≤ Randomized.randProb t (fun w => N.haltRun x w = some [true])) ∧
    (x ∉ L → ∀ w : List Bool, (N.tm.runWith w (N.tm.initCfg x)).state = none →
      N.outputWith x w = [false])

end Turing.FinNDTM

namespace Randomized

open Complexity Turing

/-- `RP` with expected running time: `⋃_e {L | some PTM decides L with one-sided error in
expected time c·(n^e + 1)}`. [AB09, §7.4.2] -/
def RP_ExpPTM : Set (Language Bool) :=
  ⋃ e : ℕ, {L | ∃ (c : ℕ) (N : FinNDTM Bool), N.RDecidesInExpTime L fun n => c * (n ^ e + 1)}

/-- `coRP` with expected running time: `{L | Lᶜ ∈ RP_ExpPTM}`. [AB09, §7.3 and §7.4.2] -/
def coRP_ExpPTM : Set (Language Bool) := {L | Lᶜ ∈ RP_ExpPTM}

/-- **Constant-threshold `RP` amplification**: if a polynomial-time verifier accepts members
with probability at least the constant `ρ ≤ 1` and never accepts non-members, then `K`
independent runs combined by `OR` give `InRP`, whenever `(1 − ρ)^K ≤ 1/3`.

**Proof sketch.** As `rp_error_reduction` with `K` blocks: the `OR` rejects exactly when the
vote count is `0`, of probability `(1 − s)^K ≤ (1 − ρ)^K` (`randProb_blockCount`); each block
of a non-member's coins is a genuine coin word, hence rejected. `rp_error_reduction` itself
does not apply: `InRPWeak c` demands acceptance `min (2/3) ((n+1)^{-c}) = 2/3` at `n = 0`,
which a constant `ρ < 2/3` need not meet. -/
theorem InRPWith.inRP_of_const {ρ : ℚ} {K : ℕ} (hK : (1 - ρ) ^ K ≤ 1/3)
    {L : Language Bool} (h : InRPWith (fun _ => ρ) L) : InRP polyTimeModel L := by
  obtain ⟨M, a, k, hM, hprop⟩ := h
  refine ⟨anyVerifier M (polyLen a k) (polyLen K 0), K * a, k,
    polyTimeModel_closedUnderAny M a k K 0 hM, fun x => ?_⟩
  have hlen : polyLen (K * a) k x.length = polyLen K 0 x.length * polyLen a k x.length := by
    unfold polyLen
    ring
  rw [hlen]
  set q := polyLen a k x.length with hq
  set K' := polyLen K 0 x.length with hK'
  have hKK : K' = K := by simp [hK', polyLen]
  constructor
  · intro hx
    set s := randProb q (fun l => M x l = true) with hs
    have hacc : randProb (K' * q)
        (fun l => anyVerifier M (polyLen a k) (polyLen K 0) x l = true) = 1 - (1 - s) ^ K' := by
      have h0 := randProb_blockCount q (M x) K' 0 (Nat.zero_le _)
      simp only [Nat.choose_zero_right, Nat.cast_one, pow_zero, one_mul,
        Nat.sub_zero] at h0
      rw [randProb_congr (B := fun l => ¬ (blockCount q K' (M x) l = 0)) fun r => by
        simp only [anyVerifier, blockCount, List.any_eq_true, ← Nat.pos_iff_ne_zero,
          List.countP_pos_iff, hq, hK'], randProb_not, h0]
    rw [hacc, hKK]
    have hs1 : s ≤ 1 := randProb_le_one
    have hsρ : ρ ≤ s := (hprop x).1 hx
    have hpow : (1 - s) ^ K ≤ (1 - ρ) ^ K := pow_le_pow_left₀ (by linarith) (by linarith) K
    linarith
  · intro hx r
    have hl : (List.ofFn r).length = K' * q := List.length_ofFn
    unfold anyVerifier
    rw [List.any_eq_false]
    intro i hi
    rw [List.mem_range, ← hK'] at hi
    have hiq : i * q + q ≤ K' * q := by
      have := Nat.mul_le_mul_right q (Nat.succ_le_of_lt hi)
      rwa [Nat.succ_mul] at this
    have hb : (((List.ofFn r).drop (i * q)).take q).length = q := by
      rw [List.length_take, List.length_drop, hl]
      omega
    obtain ⟨r', hr'⟩ := exists_ofFn_eq hb
    rw [← hq, hr', (hprop x).2 hx r']
    decide

/-- **Expected time ⇒ `RP`** [AB09, §7.4.2]: a one-sided-error PTM with expected time
`c(n^e + 1)` gives an `InRP polyTimeModel` verifier.

**Proof sketch.** With `B = c(|x|^e + 1)` and `Q = 200c(|x|+1)^e ≥ 100 B`, the choice-word
verifier for `[1]` at length `Q` accepts exactly the coin words on which `N` has halted with
output `[1]`. On non-members no halted branch outputs `[1]`, so it never accepts; on members
Markov truncation (`haltProb_le_truncate`, `haltProb_mono`) gives acceptance
`≥ 2/3 − 1/100 ≥ 5/8`. Two `OR` votes (`InRPWith.inRP_of_const`, `(3/8)² ≤ 1/3`) restore
`2/3`. -/
theorem inRP_of_mem_RP_ExpPTM {L : Language Bool} (h : L ∈ RP_ExpPTM) :
    InRP polyTimeModel L := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨e, c, N, hN⟩ := Set.mem_iUnion.mp h
  obtain ⟨V, hVP, hV⟩ := exists_choiceVerifier_mem_P N (200 * c) e
  refine InRPWith.inRP_of_const (ρ := 5/8) (K := 2) (by norm_num)
    ⟨fun x r => MultiTapeTM.indicator V (x ++ r), 200 * c, e, eff_append_mem hVP, fun x => ?_⟩
  have hNx := hN x
  dsimp only at hNx
  obtain ⟨hexp, hin, hout⟩ := hNx
  set B := c * (x.length ^ e + 1)
  set Q := polyLen (200 * c) e x.length
  have hBQ : 100 * B ≤ Q := by
    have := choiceBudget_le (100 * c) e x.length
    simp only [Q, B, polyLen] at this ⊢
    nlinarith [this]
  have hacc : ∀ r : Fin Q → Bool, MultiTapeTM.indicator V (x ++ List.ofFn r) = true ↔
      N.haltRun x (List.ofFn r) = some [true] := fun r => by
    rw [indicator_eq_true_iff]
    exact (hV x _ List.length_ofFn).trans FinNDTM.haltRun_eq_some_iff.symm
  refine ⟨fun hx => ?_, fun hx r => ?_⟩
  · have hge : 5 / 8 ≤ randProb Q (fun w => N.haltRun x w = some [true]) := by
      by_contra hlt
      push_neg at hlt
      obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := hin hx (2 / 3 - 1 / 100 - 5 / 8) (by norm_num)
      have h1 := FinNDTM.haltProb_le_truncate hexp [true] t
      have h2 := FinNDTM.haltProb_mono (N := N) (x := x) [true] hBQ
      linarith
    exact le_trans hge (randProb_mono fun r hr => (hacc r).mpr hr)
  · show MultiTapeTM.indicator V (x ++ List.ofFn r) = false
    cases hi : MultiTapeTM.indicator V (x ++ List.ofFn r)
    · rfl
    · obtain ⟨hhalt, htrue⟩ := FinNDTM.haltRun_eq_some_iff.mp ((hacc r).mp hi)
      rw [hout hx _ hhalt] at htrue
      exact absurd htrue (by decide)

/-- A worst-case one-sided-error PTM is an expected-time one. [AB09, §7.4.2]

**Proof sketch.** Halting within `T` gives `E[T_{N,x}] ≤ T` (`expTimeLe_of_haltsWithin`) and
`Pr_T[halted with 1] = Pr[N(x) = 1]`. A halted branch `w` of a non-member keeps its output
when padded to length `≥ T` (`haltRun_isPrefixStable`), and that output is the one of the
first `T` coins, which is `[0]`. -/
theorem RP_PTM_subset_RP_ExpPTM : RP_PTM ⊆ RP_ExpPTM := by
  intro L h
  obtain ⟨e, c, N, hN⟩ := Set.mem_iUnion.mp h
  refine Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨e, c, N, fun x => ?_⟩
  have hNx := hN x
  dsimp only at hNx
  obtain ⟨hhalt, hin, hout⟩ := hNx
  set T := c * (x.length ^ e + 1)
  refine ⟨FinNDTM.expTimeLe_of_haltsWithin hhalt, fun hx ε hε => ⟨T, ?_⟩, fun hx w hw => ?_⟩
  · have heq : randProb T (fun w => N.haltRun x w = some [true]) = N.outputProb x T [true] :=
      randProb_congr fun r => by
        rw [FinNDTM.haltRun_eq_some_iff]
        exact ⟨fun h => h.2, fun h => ⟨hhalt _ List.length_ofFn, h⟩⟩
    rw [heq]
    linarith [hin hx]
  · have hw' : N.haltRun x w = some (N.outputWith x w) :=
      FinNDTM.haltRun_eq_some_iff.mpr ⟨hw, rfl⟩
    set u := w ++ List.replicate (T - w.length) false with hu_def
    have hu := FinNDTM.haltRun_eq_some_iff.mp
      (N.haltRun_isPrefixStable x w (List.replicate (T - w.length) false) _ hw')
    have hTu : T ≤ u.length := by
      simp only [u, List.length_append, List.length_replicate]
      omega
    have htake : N.outputWith x u = N.outputWith x (u.take T) := by
      unfold FinNDTM.outputWith
      rw [FinNDTM.runWith_eq_runWith_take hhalt hTu]
    rw [← hu.2, htake]
    exact hout hx _ (List.length_take_of_le hTu)

/-- **Expected time gives the same `RP`** [AB09, §7.4.2]. -/
theorem RP_ExpPTM_eq_RP_PTM : RP_ExpPTM = RP_PTM :=
  Set.Subset.antisymm (fun L h => (mem_RP_PTM_iff L).mpr (inRP_of_mem_RP_ExpPTM h))
    RP_PTM_subset_RP_ExpPTM

/-- **Expected time gives the same `coRP`** [AB09, §7.4.2]. -/
theorem coRP_ExpPTM_eq_coRP_PTM : coRP_ExpPTM = coRP_PTM :=
  Set.ext fun L => show Lᶜ ∈ RP_ExpPTM ↔ Lᶜ ∈ RP_PTM by rw [RP_ExpPTM_eq_RP_PTM]

end Randomized

import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Inclusions
import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.RandomBits

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Randomized reductions and BP·NP

Randomized polynomial-time reductions and the class `BP·NP` of [AB09, §7.6, p. 138];
`BP·NP ⊆ NP/poly` [AB09, Exercise 7.7] is in `TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.NPPoly`.
Probabilities are exact counting ratios (`Randomized.randProb`); `BPP` is the certificate class
`Randomized.InBPP polyTimeModel`.

## Main definitions

* `Randomized.RandReducible` (notation `B ≤ᵣ C`) — [AB09, Def 7.16].
* `Randomized.BPNP` — `BP·NP = {L | L ≤ᵣ 3SAT}` [AB09, Def 7.17].
* `Randomized.InBPPAt` — `BPP` with success threshold `p`.

## Main results

* `Randomized.InBPP.of_randReducible` — `C ∈ BPP`, `B ≤ᵣ C` ⇒ `B ∈ BPP` [AB09, §7.6].
* `Randomized.RandReducible.of_polyTimeReducible` — `≤ₚ ⊆ ≤ᵣ`;
  `Randomized.RandReducible.of_polyTimeReducible_left` — `A ≤ₚ B ≤ᵣ C ⇒ A ≤ᵣ C`.
* `Randomized.NP_subset_BPNP` — `NP ⊆ BP·NP` [AB09, §7.6].
* `Randomized.InBPPAt.amplify` — majority amplification with a constant number of votes.

## Divergences

* **Certificate form of Def 7.16.** The book's probabilistic transducer `M` is a
  polynomial-time `f` on `pairEncode x r` with `r ∈ {0,1}^{polyLen a k |x|}`, as Def 7.3 does
  for `BPP`. The printed event `B(M(x)) = C(x)` has `B` and `C` swapped; we use
  `C(f(x, r)) = B(x)`, the reading under which the remark and Def 7.17 hold.
* **Transitivity** is not claimed: the book notes `≤ᵣ` is not transitive. Composition with a
  Karp reduction on either side is.
* `3SAT` is `Complexity.SAT3`, with that file's encoding conventions.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009.
-/

namespace Randomized

open Complexity Turing

/-! ### `BPP` with an arbitrary success threshold -/

variable (E : VerifierModel)

/-- `L` is decided by an `E`-efficient verifier with success probability at least `p` on every
input; `InBPP E` is the case `p = 2/3`. [AB09, Def 7.3] -/
def InBPPAt (p : ℚ) (L : Language Bool) : Prop :=
  ∃ (M : List Bool → List Bool → Bool) (a k : ℕ),
    E.Eff (boolVerifier M) ∧
    ∀ x : List Bool,
      (x ∈ L → p ≤ randProb (polyLen a k x.length) fun r => M x r = true) ∧
      (x ∉ L → p ≤ randProb (polyLen a k x.length) fun r => M x r = false)

variable {E}

/-- Lowering the threshold keeps the same verifier. -/
theorem InBPPAt.mono {p p' : ℚ} {L : Language Bool} (h : InBPPAt E p L) (hp : p' ≤ p) :
    InBPPAt E p' L := by
  obtain ⟨M, a, k, hM, hL⟩ := h
  exact ⟨M, a, k, hM, fun x => ⟨fun hx => hp.trans ((hL x).1 hx),
    fun hx => hp.trans ((hL x).2 hx)⟩⟩

/-- `InBPP` is `InBPPAt` at threshold `2/3`. -/
theorem inBPP_iff_inBPPAt (L : Language Bool) : InBPP E L ↔ InBPPAt E (2/3) L := Iff.rfl

/-- **Constant-factor majority amplification**: a constant number `K` of independent runs
and a majority vote turn success probability `1/2 + ε` into `1 − η` whenever
`2(1 − 4ε²)^{⌊K/2⌋} ≤ η`. [AB09, Thm 7.10] (with a constant repetition count, from any
success `1/2 + ε`; `amplify_concrete` starts from success `2/3`)

**Proof sketch.** As `bpp_error_reduction`: the majority errs exactly when at least half of
the `K` blocks err, and each block errs with probability at most `1/2 − ε`, so the binomial
tail bound `randProb_tail_le` applies; the vote counts of a test and of its negation add up
to `K` (`blockCount_add_not`). -/
theorem InBPPAt.amplify (hMaj : ClosedUnderMajority E) (K : ℕ) {ε η : ℚ} (hε : 0 ≤ ε)
    (hK : 2 * (1 - 4 * ε ^ 2) ^ (K / 2) ≤ η) {L : Language Bool}
    (h : InBPPAt E (1/2 + ε) L) : InBPPAt E (1 - η) L := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨M, a, k, hM, hprop⟩ := h
  refine ⟨majorityVerifier M (polyLen a k) (polyLen K 0), K * a, k,
    hMaj M a k K 0 hM, fun x => ?_⟩
  set q := polyLen a k x.length with hq
  have hK0 : polyLen K 0 x.length = K := by simp [polyLen]
  have hlen : polyLen (K * a) k x.length = K * q := by
    simp only [hq, polyLen]
    ring
  have hmaj : ∀ l : List Bool,
      majorityVerifier M (polyLen a k) (polyLen K 0) x l = true ↔
        K < 2 * blockCount q K (M x) l := by
    intro l
    show decide (polyLen K 0 x.length < 2 * blockCount q (polyLen K 0 x.length) (M x) l) = true ↔ _
    rw [decide_eq_true_iff, hK0]
  have hs_not : randProb q (fun l => (!(M x l)) = true) =
      1 - randProb q (fun l => M x l = true) := by
    rw [← randProb_bool_false]
    exact randProb_congr fun r => by simp
  rw [hlen]
  constructor
  · intro hx
    have hW := (hprop x).1 hx
    have htail := randProb_tail_le q K (fun l' => !(M x l')) hε (by rw [hs_not]; linarith)
    have hev : randProb (K * q)
        (fun l => ¬ (majorityVerifier M (polyLen a k) (polyLen K 0) x l = true)) =
        randProb (K * q) (fun l => K ≤ 2 * blockCount q K (fun l' => !(M x l')) l) :=
      randProb_congr fun r => by
        rw [hmaj]
        have := blockCount_add_not q K (M x) (List.ofFn r)
        omega
    have hnot := randProb_not (m := K * q)
      (fun l => majorityVerifier M (polyLen a k) (polyLen K 0) x l = true)
    rw [hev] at hnot
    linarith
  · intro hx
    have hW := (hprop x).2 hx
    have hst : randProb q (fun l => M x l = true) ≤ 1/2 - ε := by
      have := randProb_bool_false (m := q) (M x)
      linarith
    have htail := randProb_tail_le q K (M x) hε hst
    have hmono : randProb (K * q)
        (fun l => ¬ (majorityVerifier M (polyLen a k) (polyLen K 0) x l = false)) ≤
        randProb (K * q) (fun l => K ≤ 2 * blockCount q K (M x) l) := by
      refine randProb_mono fun r hr => ?_
      have h1 : majorityVerifier M (polyLen a k) (polyLen K 0) x (List.ofFn r) = true := by
        simpa using hr
      have := (hmaj _).mp h1
      omega
    have hnot := randProb_not (m := K * q)
      (fun l => majorityVerifier M (polyLen a k) (polyLen K 0) x l = false)
    linarith

/-- A `BPP` language has an efficient verifier erring with probability at most `1/24` on
every input (via `amplify_concrete`, error `2^{-5}`). -/
theorem InBPP.inBPPAt_23_24 (hMaj : ClosedUnderMajority E) {L : Language Bool}
    (h : InBPP E L) : InBPPAt E (23/24) L := by
  obtain ⟨M₀, a₀, k₀, hM₀, hprop₀⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨M, hM, hprop⟩ := amplify_concrete E hMaj hM₀ hprop₀ 5 0
  have hth : ∀ n, (23/24 : ℚ) ≤ 1 - (1/2) ^ polyLen 5 0 n := fun n => by
    simp only [polyLen, pow_zero, mul_one]
    norm_num
  exact ⟨M, _, _, hM, fun x => ⟨fun hx => (hth _).trans ((hprop x).1 hx),
    fun hx => (hth _).trans ((hprop x).2 hx)⟩⟩

/-- Success probability `5/8` suffices for `BPP` (`60` majority votes). -/
theorem InBPPAt.inBPP_of_5_8 (hMaj : ClosedUnderMajority E) {L : Language Bool}
    (h : InBPPAt E (5/8) L) : InBPP E L := by
  have h' : InBPPAt E (1/2 + 1/8) L := h.mono (by norm_num)
  exact (h'.amplify hMaj 60 (by norm_num) (η := 1/3) (by norm_num)).mono (by norm_num)

/-! ### Randomized reductions -/

open Classical in
/-- **Randomized reduction** `B ≤ᵣ C` [AB09, Def 7.16]: a polynomial-time computable `f`,
run on the input `x` paired with a random string `r` of length `polyLen a k |x|`, satisfies
`Pr_r[f(x, r) ∈ C ↔ x ∈ B] ≥ 2/3`. -/
def RandReducible (B C : Language Bool) : Prop :=
  ∃ (f : List Bool → List Bool) (a k : ℕ), PolyTimeComputable f ∧
    ∀ x : List Bool,
      2/3 ≤ randProb (polyLen a k x.length) fun r => (f (Turing.pairEncode x r) ∈ C ↔ x ∈ B)

@[inherit_doc] scoped infix:50 " ≤ᵣ " => RandReducible

/-- A Karp reduction is a randomized reduction that ignores its coins. [AB09, §7.6] -/
theorem RandReducible.of_polyTimeReducible {B C : Language Bool} (h : B ≤ₚ C) : B ≤ᵣ C := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨f, hf, hfB⟩ := h
  refine ⟨fun z => f (pairFstD z), 0, 0, hf.comp polyTimeComputable_pairFstD, fun x => ?_⟩
  rw [randProb_congr (B := fun _ => True) fun r => by simp [hfB x], randProb_true]
  norm_num

/-- A Karp reduction followed by a randomized reduction is a randomized reduction:
`A ≤ₚ B` and `B ≤ᵣ C` give `A ≤ᵣ C`.

**Proof sketch.** Run the randomized reduction on `g x` with the first
`polyLen a k |g x|` coins; that length is bounded by a schedule in `|x|` because `|g x|` is
polynomial in `|x|`, and surplus coins are ignored (`randProb_take`). -/
theorem RandReducible.of_polyTimeReducible_left {A B C : Language Bool} (h₁ : A ≤ₚ B)
    (h₂ : B ≤ᵣ C) : A ≤ᵣ C := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨g, hg, hgA⟩ := h₁
  obtain ⟨f, a, k, hf, hprob⟩ := h₂
  obtain ⟨Cg, cg, hCg⟩ := hg.output_length_le
  refine ⟨fun z => f (sliceTake a k (Turing.pairEncode (g (pairFstD z)) (pairSndD z))),
    a * (Cg + 1) ^ k, cg * k, hf.comp ((polyTimeComputable_sliceTake a k).comp
      ((hg.comp polyTimeComputable_pairFstD).pairEncode polyTimeComputable_pairSndD)),
    fun x => ?_⟩
  have hle : polyLen a k (g x).length ≤ polyLen (a * (Cg + 1) ^ k) (cg * k) x.length := by
    have hp : 1 ≤ (x.length + 1) ^ cg := Nat.one_le_pow _ _ (Nat.succ_pos _)
    have h1 : (g x).length + 1 ≤ (Cg + 1) * (x.length + 1) ^ cg := by
      nlinarith [hCg x]
    calc polyLen a k (g x).length = a * ((g x).length + 1) ^ k := rfl
      _ ≤ a * ((Cg + 1) * (x.length + 1) ^ cg) ^ k :=
          Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (Nat.pow_le_pow_left h1 k)
      _ = polyLen (a * (Cg + 1) ^ k) (cg * k) x.length := by
          unfold polyLen
          rw [mul_pow, ← pow_mul]
          ring
  have key := randProb_take hle (fun s => (f (Turing.pairEncode (g x) s) ∈ C ↔ g x ∈ B))
  refine (hprob (g x)).trans (le_of_eq ?_)
  rw [← key]
  exact randProb_congr fun r => by
    simp [sliceTake, hgA x]

/-- The composite of the reduction's first stage and a second-stage slice: on
`pairEncode x t` it is `pairEncode y (t'.take (polyLen a₂ k₂ |y|))`, where `t'` drops the first
`polyLen a₁ k₁ |x|` bits of `t` and `y = f (pairEncode x (t.take (polyLen a₁ k₁ |x|)))`. -/
def composeMap (a₁ k₁ a₂ k₂ : ℕ) (f : List Bool → List Bool) (z : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  sliceTake a₂ k₂ (Turing.pairEncode (f (sliceTake a₁ k₁ z)) (pairSndD (sliceDrop a₁ k₁ z)))

/-- `composeMap` on a pair, unfolded. -/
theorem composeMap_pairEncode (a₁ k₁ a₂ k₂ : ℕ) (f : List Bool → List Bool) (x t : List Bool) :
    composeMap a₁ k₁ a₂ k₂ f (Turing.pairEncode x t) =
      Turing.pairEncode (f (Turing.pairEncode x (t.take (polyLen a₁ k₁ x.length))))
        ((t.drop (polyLen a₁ k₁ x.length)).take (polyLen a₂ k₂
          (f (Turing.pairEncode x (t.take (polyLen a₁ k₁ x.length)))).length)) := by
  simp [composeMap, sliceTake, sliceDrop]

/-- `composeMap` is polynomial-time computable when `f` is. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_composeMap (a₁ k₁ a₂ k₂ : ℕ) {f : List Bool → List Bool}
    (hf : PolyTimeComputable f) : PolyTimeComputable (composeMap a₁ k₁ a₂ k₂ f) :=
  (polyTimeComputable_sliceTake a₂ k₂).comp
    ((hf.comp (polyTimeComputable_sliceTake a₁ k₁)).pairEncode
      (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp (polyTimeComputable_sliceDrop a₁ k₁)))

/-- A polynomial schedule evaluated at the output length of a polynomially bounded `f` on
`pairEncode x r`, with `|r| = polyLen a₁ k₁ |x|`, is bounded by a schedule in `|x|`.

**Proof sketch.** `|pairEncode x r| + 1 = 2|x| + 3 + a₁(|x|+1)^{k₁} ≤ (a₁+3)(|x|+1)^{k₁+1}`;
feed this through the output bound of `f` and then through `polyLen a₂ k₂`. -/
theorem polyLen_length_pairEncode_le {f : List Bool → List Bool} {C c : ℕ}
    (hC : ∀ z, (f z).length ≤ C * (z.length + 1) ^ c) (a₁ k₁ a₂ k₂ : ℕ) {x r : List Bool}
    (hr : r.length = polyLen a₁ k₁ x.length) :
    polyLen a₂ k₂ (f (Turing.pairEncode x r)).length ≤
      polyLen (a₂ * ((C + 1) * (a₁ + 3) ^ c) ^ k₂) ((k₁ + 1) * c * k₂) x.length := by
  set n := x.length
  have hN : 0 < n + 1 := Nat.succ_pos n
  have hP : (Turing.pairEncode x r).length + 1 ≤ (a₁ + 3) * (n + 1) ^ (k₁ + 1) := by
    rw [length_pairEncode, hr]
    have h1 : n + 1 ≤ (n + 1) ^ (k₁ + 1) := Nat.le_self_pow (Nat.succ_ne_zero k₁) _
    have h2 : (n + 1) ^ k₁ ≤ (n + 1) ^ (k₁ + 1) := Nat.pow_le_pow_right hN (Nat.le_succ k₁)
    unfold polyLen
    nlinarith [Nat.mul_le_mul_left a₁ h2]
  have hf1 : (f (Turing.pairEncode x r)).length + 1 ≤
      (C + 1) * (a₁ + 3) ^ c * (n + 1) ^ ((k₁ + 1) * c) := by
    have hpos : 1 ≤ ((Turing.pairEncode x r).length + 1) ^ c := Nat.one_le_pow _ _ (Nat.succ_pos _)
    calc (f (Turing.pairEncode x r)).length + 1
        ≤ C * ((Turing.pairEncode x r).length + 1) ^ c +
            ((Turing.pairEncode x r).length + 1) ^ c := Nat.add_le_add (hC _) hpos
      _ = (C + 1) * ((Turing.pairEncode x r).length + 1) ^ c := by ring
      _ ≤ (C + 1) * ((a₁ + 3) * (n + 1) ^ (k₁ + 1)) ^ c :=
          Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (Nat.pow_le_pow_left hP c)
      _ = (C + 1) * (a₁ + 3) ^ c * (n + 1) ^ ((k₁ + 1) * c) := by
          rw [mul_pow, ← pow_mul]
          ring
  calc polyLen a₂ k₂ (f (Turing.pairEncode x r)).length
      = a₂ * ((f (Turing.pairEncode x r)).length + 1) ^ k₂ := rfl
    _ ≤ a₂ * ((C + 1) * (a₁ + 3) ^ c * (n + 1) ^ ((k₁ + 1) * c)) ^ k₂ :=
        Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (Nat.pow_le_pow_left hf1 k₂)
    _ = polyLen (a₂ * ((C + 1) * (a₁ + 3) ^ c) ^ k₂) ((k₁ + 1) * c * k₂) n := by
        unfold polyLen
        rw [mul_pow, ← pow_mul]
        ring

/-- **`BPP` is closed under randomized reductions** [AB09, §7.6, remark after Def 7.16]: if
`C ∈ BPP` and `B ≤ᵣ C` then `B ∈ BPP` (certificate form over `polyTimeModel`).

**Proof sketch.** Composing the reduction (success `2/3`) with a `2/3`-verifier for `C`
could leave success only `4/9`, so first amplify the verifier for `C` to error `1/24`
(`InBPP.inBPPAt_23_24`). Run the reduction on the first `polyLen a₁ k₁ |x|` coins and the
amplified verifier on `y = f(x, r₁)` with the next coins; the coin length for `y` is bounded
by a schedule in `|x|` (`polyLen_length_pairEncode_le`), and surplus coins are ignored
(`randProb_take`). Conditioning on the first segment (`randProb_append_ge`), the composite
is correct with probability at least `2/3 · 23/24 > 5/8`, and a constant majority vote
(`InBPPAt.inBPP_of_5_8`) restores `2/3`. The composite is polynomial-time because its answer
sets are preimages of the verifier's under `composeMap`. -/
theorem InBPP.of_randReducible {B C : Language Bool} (hred : B ≤ᵣ C)
    (hC : InBPP polyTimeModel C) : InBPP polyTimeModel B := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨f, a₁, k₁, hf, hprob⟩ := hred
  obtain ⟨Cf, cf, hCf⟩ := hf.output_length_le
  obtain ⟨M, a₂, k₂, ⟨V₁, V₀, hV₁, hV₀, hM⟩, hMC⟩ :=
    hC.inBPPAt_23_24 polyTimeModel_closedUnderMajority
  set A := a₂ * ((Cf + 1) * (a₁ + 3) ^ cf) ^ k₂
  set K := (k₁ + 1) * cf * k₂
  -- the composite verifier
  let V : List Bool → List Bool → Bool := fun x t =>
    M (f (Turing.pairEncode x (t.take (polyLen a₁ k₁ x.length))))
      ((t.drop (polyLen a₁ k₁ x.length)).take (polyLen a₂ k₂
        (f (Turing.pairEncode x (t.take (polyLen a₁ k₁ x.length)))).length))
  have hEff : polyTimeModel.Eff (boolVerifier V) := by
    refine ⟨composeMap a₁ k₁ a₂ k₂ f ⁻¹' V₁, composeMap a₁ k₁ a₂ k₂ f ⁻¹' V₀,
      preimage_mem_P hV₁ (polyTimeComputable_composeMap _ _ _ _ hf),
      preimage_mem_P hV₀ (polyTimeComputable_composeMap _ _ _ _ hf), fun x t => ?_⟩
    show (_ ↔ composeMap a₁ k₁ a₂ k₂ f (Turing.pairEncode x t) ∈ V₁) ∧
      (_ ↔ composeMap a₁ k₁ a₂ k₂ f (Turing.pairEncode x t) ∈ V₀)
    rw [composeMap_pairEncode]
    exact hM _ _
  refine InBPPAt.inBPP_of_5_8 polyTimeModel_closedUnderMajority
    ⟨V, a₁ + A, k₁ + K, hEff, fun x => ?_⟩
  set n := x.length
  set q := polyLen a₁ k₁ n
  have hq : q + polyLen A K n ≤ polyLen (a₁ + A) (k₁ + K) n := by
    have h1 : (n + 1) ^ k₁ ≤ (n + 1) ^ (k₁ + K) := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (Nat.succ_pos n) (by omega)
    have h2 : (n + 1) ^ K ≤ (n + 1) ^ (k₁ + K) := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (Nat.succ_pos n) (by omega)
    simp only [q, polyLen]
    nlinarith [Nat.mul_le_mul_left a₁ h1, Nat.mul_le_mul_left A h2]
  obtain ⟨m₂, hm₂⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le (le_trans (Nat.le_add_right q _) hq)
  have hm₂' : polyLen A K n ≤ m₂ := by omega
  -- the second-stage coin length fits in the second segment
  have hfit : ∀ u : Fin q → Bool,
      polyLen a₂ k₂ (f (Turing.pairEncode x (List.ofFn u))).length ≤ m₂ := fun u =>
    (polyLen_length_pairEncode_le hCf a₁ k₁ a₂ k₂ (by simp [q, n])).trans hm₂'
  -- one bound for both answers
  have key : ∀ b : Bool, (∀ y, (y ∈ C ↔ x ∈ B) →
      23/24 ≤ randProb (polyLen a₂ k₂ y.length) fun s => M y s = b) →
      5/8 ≤ randProb (polyLen (a₁ + A) (k₁ + K) n) fun t => V x t = b := by
    intro b hb
    rw [hm₂]
    have hA : 2/3 ≤ randProb q (fun r => (f (Turing.pairEncode x r) ∈ C ↔ x ∈ B)) :=
      (hprob x).trans_eq (randProb_congr fun _ => Iff.rfl)
    have hlow := randProb_append_ge q m₂
      (fun r => (f (Turing.pairEncode x r) ∈ C ↔ x ∈ B))
      (fun r s => M (f (Turing.pairEncode x r))
        (s.take (polyLen a₂ k₂ (f (Turing.pairEncode x r)).length)) = b)
      (ε := 23/24) (fun u hu => by
        refine le_of_le_of_eq (hb _ hu) ?_
        exact (randProb_take (hfit u)
          (fun s => M (f (Turing.pairEncode x (List.ofFn u))) s = b)).symm)
    have heq : randProb (q + m₂) (fun t => V x t = b) =
        randProb (q + m₂) (fun t => M (f (Turing.pairEncode x (t.take q)))
          ((t.drop q).take (polyLen a₂ k₂ (f (Turing.pairEncode x (t.take q))).length)) = b) :=
      randProb_congr fun _ => Iff.rfl
    rw [heq]
    nlinarith
  refine ⟨fun hx => key true fun y hy => (hMC y).1 (hy.mpr hx),
    fun hx => key false fun y hy => (hMC y).2 fun hyC => hx (hy.mp hyC)⟩

/-! ### `BP·NP` -/

/-- **`BP·NP`** [AB09, Def 7.17]: the languages randomly reducible to `3SAT`. -/
def BPNP : Set (Language Bool) :=
  {L | L ≤ᵣ SAT3}

/-- **`NP ⊆ BP·NP`**: a Karp reduction to `3SAT` (Cook–Levin) is a randomized one.
[AB09, §7.6] -/
theorem NP_subset_BPNP : NP ⊆ BPNP :=
  fun L hL => RandReducible.of_polyTimeReducible (SAT3_NPHard L hL)

end Randomized

import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.NPPoly
import TCSlib.Complexity.CircuitComplexity.KarpLiptonPrefix
import TCSlib.Complexity.CircuitComplexity.CircuitEval
import TCSlib.Complexity.CircuitComplexity.Uniform
import TCSlib.Complexity.PolyHierarchy.Collapse

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Yap's theorem and [AB09, Exercise 7.8]

Yap's theorem, the `NP/poly` analogue of Karp–Lipton: **if `coNP ⊆ NP/poly` then
`PH = Σ₃ᵖ`**. With `Randomized.coNP_subset_NPPoly_of_compl_SAT3_mem_BPNP` it gives
[AB09, Exercise 7.8]: if `3SATᶜ ∈ BP·NP` then `PH = Σ₃ᵖ`.

We show `Π₃ᵖ ⊆ Σ₃ᵖ` and collapse ([AB09, Theorem 5.4]). Write
`x ∈ L ⟺ ∀ u ∃ v, ⟨⟨x, u⟩, v⟩ ∈ K` with `K ∈ coNP`, `z ∈ Kᶜ ⟺ ∃ r, ⟨z, r⟩ ∈ R`, `R ∈ P`,
and let `D` be `NP/poly` circuits for `K`. The `Σ₃ᵖ` formula guesses the description `U` of
`D` at the length `N(|x|)` of the `z = ⟨⟨x, u⟩, v⟩`, and checks, through `CVAL` queries,

`∃ U ∀ (u, v', w', r) ∃ (v, w)`: if `|u|` is right then `U` accepts `(⟨⟨x, u⟩, v⟩, w)` and
it is *not* the case that `U` accepts `(⟨⟨x, u⟩, v'⟩, w')` while `r` refutes `⟨⟨x, u⟩, v'⟩ ∈ K`.

The second clause makes every accepted `z` lie in `K` whatever `U` is (soundness, `sound`);
the true circuit passes both clauses when `x ∈ L` (completeness, `complete`).

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.Yap.Query` — one evaluation of the guessed circuit.
* `Complexity.Yap.Data` — the constants of the construction; `Data.Core`, `Data.Check` —
  the checks; `Data.checkLang` (`P`), `Data.badLang` (`coNP`), `Data.innerLang` (`Π₂ᵖ`).

## Main results

* `Complexity.Yap.query_append_iff` — a query to an `NP/poly` circuit's description.
* `Complexity.Yap.mem_SigmaP_succ_of_exists_le` — a length-bounded `∃` over `Πᵢᵖ` is `Σᵢ₊₁ᵖ`.
* `Complexity.Yap.Data.checkLang_mem_P` — the check is polynomial-time.
* `Complexity.Yap.sound`, `Complexity.Yap.complete`.
* `Complexity.PiP_three_subset_SigmaP_three_of_coNP_subset_NPPoly` — `Π₃ᵖ ⊆ Σ₃ᵖ`.
* `Complexity.PH_eq_SigmaP_three_of_coNP_subset_NPPoly` — Yap's theorem.
* `Randomized.PH_eq_SigmaP_three_of_compl_SAT3_mem_BPNP` — [AB09, Exercise 7.8].

## Divergences

* **Exercise 7.8's hypothesis** is `3SATᶜ ∈ BP·NP`: the overbar on `3SAT` is lost in the
  printed text, and `3SAT ∈ BP·NP` holds outright (see `Randomized/NPPoly.lean`).
* **Self-consistency instead of a correctness proof for the circuit**, as in
  `CircuitComplexity/KarpLipton.lean` ([AB09, Theorem 6.19]): the `∀` block checks that no
  accepted instance is refuted, rather than comparing the circuit with `K` on all inputs.
* **Length bounds.** The universal and existential blocks are checked against an explicit
  polynomial bound inside the verifier, so the inner languages accept only bounded blocks.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (Theorem 5.4; Theorem 6.19; Exercises 7.7–7.8, p. 142.)
* [Yap83] C.-K. Yap, *Some consequences of non-uniform conditions on uniform classes*,
  Theoretical Computer Science 26 (1983), 287–300. Theorem numbering follows the standard
  citation of the result (`coNP ⊆ NP/poly ⇒ PH = Σ₃ᵖ` is cited as its Theorem 2).
-/

namespace Complexity.Yap

open Turing BoolCircuit Complexity.PolyHierarchy

/-! ### Querying a guessed circuit -/

/-- **One query to a guessed circuit**: the description `d` accepts `q`, i.e.
`⟨d, q⟩ ∈ CVAL`. -/
def Query (d q : List Bool) : Prop := pairEncode d q ∈ CVAL

/-- An accepted query is no longer than the description (the description lists the
inputs). -/
theorem length_le_of_query {d q : List Bool} (h : Query d q) : q.length ≤ d.length := by
  obtain ⟨x, C, -, -, heq⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := Prod.mk.inj (pairEncode_injective (a₁ := (d, q)) (a₂ := (_, _)) heq)
  rw [h1, h2]
  exact le_trans (Nat.le_add_right _ _) C.size_le_length_encode

/-- Circuits with the same description agree on inputs with the same bits. -/
theorem eval_eq_of_encode_eq {n₁ n₂ : ℕ} {C₁ : DAGCircuit n₁} {C₂ : DAGCircuit n₂}
    (h : C₁.encode = C₂.encode) {x₁ : Fin n₁ → Bool} {x₂ : Fin n₂ → Bool}
    (hx : List.ofFn x₁ = List.ofFn x₂) : C₁.eval x₁ = C₂.eval x₂ := by
  obtain ⟨-, hg, ho⟩ := DAGCircuit.eq_of_encode_eq h
  simp only [DAGCircuit.eval, DAGCircuit.values, hg, ho, hx]

/-- **A query to a known circuit's description** is an evaluation: `C` accepts `q` iff
`q` is an input of `C` on which it outputs `1`. -/
theorem query_encode_iff {n : ℕ} (C : DAGCircuit n) (hC : C.IsFaninTwo) (q : List Bool) :
    Query C.encode q ↔ ∃ x : Fin n → Bool, List.ofFn x = q ∧ C.eval x = true := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨q', C', -, hev, heq⟩
    obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := Prod.mk.inj (pairEncode_injective (a₁ := (_, _)) (a₂ := (_, _)) heq)
    have hn : n = q'.length := (DAGCircuit.eq_of_encode_eq h1).1
    have hq := (List.ofFn_congr hn.symm q'.get).symm
    refine ⟨fun i => q'.get (i.cast hn), by rw [h2]; exact hq.trans (List.ofFn_get q'), ?_⟩
    rw [eval_eq_of_encode_eq h1 hq]
    exact hev
  · rintro ⟨x, rfl, hev⟩
    have hn : n = (List.ofFn x).length := (List.length_ofFn).symm
    have key : ∀ (m : ℕ) (C' : DAGCircuit m) (q : List Bool) (h : m = q.length),
        C'.IsFaninTwo → C'.eval (fun i => q.get (i.cast h)) = true → Query C'.encode q := by
      intro m C' q h hC' hev'
      subst h
      exact ⟨q, C', hC', by simpa using hev', rfl⟩
    refine key n C _ hn hC ?_
    rw [eval_eq_of_encode_eq rfl ((List.ofFn_congr hn.symm _).symm.trans (List.ofFn_get _))]
    exact hev

/-- **A query to an `NP/poly` circuit**: for `|z| = N`, the description of the circuit
`D_N` (on `z` and a certificate) accepts `z ++ w` iff `w` is a certificate making
`D_{|z|}` accept `z`. -/
theorem query_append_iff {m : ℕ → ℕ} (D : (n : ℕ) → DAGCircuit (n + m n))
    (hD : ∀ n, (D n).IsFaninTwo) {N : ℕ} (z w : List Bool) (hz : z.length = N) :
    Query (D N).encode (z ++ w) ↔ ∃ y : Fin (m z.length) → Bool,
      w = List.ofFn y ∧ (D z.length).eval (Fin.append z.get y) = true := by
  subst hz
  rw [query_encode_iff _ (hD _)]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨x, hx, hev⟩
    have hxab : x = Fin.append (fun i => x (Fin.castAdd (m z.length) i))
        (fun j => x (Fin.natAdd z.length j)) := Fin.append_castAdd_natAdd.symm
    rw [hxab, List.ofFn_fin_append] at hx
    rw [hxab] at hev
    obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := List.append_inj hx (by simp)
    have hz : (fun i => x (Fin.castAdd (m z.length) i)) = z.get :=
      List.ofFn_injective (h1.trans (List.ofFn_get z).symm)
    rw [hz] at hev
    exact ⟨_, h2.symm, hev⟩
  · rintro ⟨y, rfl, hev⟩
    exact ⟨_, by rw [List.ofFn_fin_append, List.ofFn_get], hev⟩

/-! ### A length-bounded existential block -/

/-- **A length-bounded `∃` over a `Πᵢᵖ` language is `Σᵢ₊₁ᵖ`**: if every `⟨x, u⟩ ∈ L'`
gives `x ∈ L`, and every `x ∈ L` has such a `u` of length at most `B (|x|+1)^b`, then
`L ∈ Σᵢ₊₁ᵖ`. The witness is padded to the exact length `(B+1)(|x|+1)^b` as `1ʳ 0 u`.

**Proof sketch.** Apply `mem_SigmaP_succ_iff` to the preimage of `L'` under
`⟨x, U⟩ ↦ ⟨x, dropMarker U⟩` (in `Πᵢᵖ` by closure under polynomial-time preimages). -/
theorem mem_SigmaP_succ_of_exists_le {i : ℕ} {L L' : Language Bool} (hL' : L' ∈ PiP i)
    (B b : ℕ) (h₁ : ∀ x u, pairEncode x u ∈ L' → x ∈ L)
    (h₂ : ∀ x ∈ L, ∃ u : List Bool, u.length ≤ B * (x.length + 1) ^ b ∧ pairEncode x u ∈ L') :
    L ∈ SigmaP (i + 1) := by
  let g : List Bool → List Bool :=
    fun z => pairEncode (pairFstD z) (KarpLipton.dropMarker (pairSndD z))
  have hgp : PolyTimeComputable g := polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.pairEncode
    (KarpLipton.polyTimeComputable_dropMarker.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD)
  refine mem_SigmaP_succ_iff.mpr ⟨B + 1, b, g ⁻¹' L', preimage_mem_PiP hL' hgp, fun x => ?_⟩
  have hg : ∀ U, g (pairEncode x U) = pairEncode x (KarpLipton.dropMarker U) := fun U => by
    simp [g]
  constructor
  · intro hx
    obtain ⟨u, hu, hmem⟩ := h₂ x hx
    have hone : 1 ≤ (x.length + 1) ^ b := Nat.one_le_pow _ _ (Nat.succ_pos _)
    have hsplit : (B + 1) * (x.length + 1) ^ b = B * (x.length + 1) ^ b + (x.length + 1) ^ b := by
      ring
    refine ⟨List.replicate ((B + 1) * (x.length + 1) ^ b - u.length - 1) true ++ false :: u,
      ?_, ?_⟩
    · simp only [List.length_append, List.length_replicate, List.length_cons]
      omega
    · show g _ ∈ L'
      rw [hg, KarpLipton.dropMarker_marker]
      exact hmem
  · rintro ⟨U, -, hU⟩
    exact h₁ x _ (by rw [Set.mem_preimage, hg] at hU; exact hU)

/-! ### The checks -/

/-- The length `N(n)` of `⟨⟨x, u⟩, v⟩` for `|x| = n`, `|u| = C₁ (n+1)^{c₁}` and
`|v| = C₂ (|⟨x, u⟩|+1)^{c₂}`. -/
def nN (C₁ c₁ C₂ c₂ n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  2 * (2 * n + 2 + C₁ * (n + 1) ^ c₁) + 2 + C₂ * (2 * n + 2 + C₁ * (n + 1) ^ c₁ + 1) ^ c₂

/-- The constants of the construction: block lengths `C₁ (n+1)^{c₁}` (for `u`) and
`C₂ (n+1)^{c₂}` (for `v`), the refutation bound `C₃ (n+1)^{c₃}` and relation `R` of `Kᶜ`,
and the bound `B (n+1)^b` on the inner blocks. -/
structure Data where
  /-- Coefficient of the first block length. -/
  C₁ : ℕ
  /-- Degree of the first block length. -/
  c₁ : ℕ
  /-- Coefficient of the second block length. -/
  C₂ : ℕ
  /-- Degree of the second block length. -/
  c₂ : ℕ
  /-- Coefficient of the refutation length. -/
  C₃ : ℕ
  /-- Degree of the refutation length. -/
  c₃ : ℕ
  /-- Coefficient of the inner block bound. -/
  B : ℕ
  /-- Degree of the inner block bound. -/
  b : ℕ
  /-- The refutation relation: `z ∉ K ⟺ ∃ r, ⟨z, r⟩ ∈ R`. -/
  R : Language Bool

namespace Data

variable (d : Data)

/-- The length of the universal block `u` for the input `x`. -/
def M₁ (x : List Bool) : ℕ := d.C₁ * (x.length + 1) ^ d.c₁

/-- The length of the existential block `v` for `y = ⟨x, u⟩`. -/
def M₂ (y : List Bool) : ℕ := d.C₂ * (y.length + 1) ^ d.c₂

/-- The length `N(|x|)` of the instances `⟨⟨x, u⟩, v⟩` of `K`. -/
def nLen (x : List Bool) : ℕ := nN d.C₁ d.c₁ d.C₂ d.c₂ x.length

/-- **A soundness failure**: `U` accepts the well-formed instance `z = ⟨⟨x, u⟩, v⟩` with
certificate `w`, while `r` refutes `z ∈ K`. -/
def SoundFail (x U u v w r : List Bool) : Prop :=
  v.length = d.M₂ (pairEncode x u) ∧ Query U (pairEncode (pairEncode x u) v ++ w) ∧
    r.length ≤ d.C₃ * ((pairEncode (pairEncode x u) v).length + 1) ^ d.c₃ ∧
    pairEncode (pairEncode (pairEncode x u) v) r ∈ d.R

/-- **A match**: `U` accepts the well-formed instance `⟨⟨x, u⟩, v⟩` with certificate `w`. -/
def Match (x U u v w : List Bool) : Prop :=
  v.length = d.M₂ (pairEncode x u) ∧ Query U (pairEncode (pairEncode x u) v ++ w)

/-- **The core check** on `x`, the guess `U`, the universal block `t = ⟨⟨u, v'⟩, ⟨w', r⟩⟩`
and the existential block `e = ⟨v, w⟩`: `|u|` is right, and either `(v', w', r)` is a
soundness failure or `(v, w)` is not a match. -/
def Core (x U t e : List Bool) : Prop :=
  (pairFstD (pairFstD t)).length = d.M₁ x ∧
    (d.SoundFail x U (pairFstD (pairFstD t)) (pairSndD (pairFstD t)) (pairFstD (pairSndD t))
        (pairSndD (pairSndD t)) ∨
      ¬ d.Match x U (pairFstD (pairFstD t)) (pairFstD e) (pairSndD e))

/-- **The full check** on `w = ⟨x, U⟩`: the universal block is bounded, and the core check. -/
def Check (w t e : List Bool) : Prop :=
  t.length ≤ d.B * (w.length + 1) ^ d.b ∧ d.Core (pairFstD w) (pairSndD w) t e

/-- **The counterexample language** (`coNP`): pairs `p = ⟨w, t⟩` such that every bounded
existential block `e` passes the check, i.e. `t` defeats the guess. -/
def badLang : Language Bool :=
  {p | ∀ e : List Bool, e.length ≤ d.B * (p.length + 1) ^ d.b →
    d.Check (pairFstD p) (pairSndD p) e}

/-- **The inner language** (`Π₂ᵖ`): the `w = ⟨x, U⟩` admitting no counterexample. -/
def innerLang : Language Bool := {w | ∀ t : List Bool, pairEncode w t ∉ d.badLang}

/-- The check language, on `⟨⟨w, t⟩, e⟩`. -/
def checkLang : Language Bool :=
  {q | d.Check (pairFstD (pairFstD q)) (pairSndD (pairFstD q)) (pairSndD q)}

/-- Membership in the counterexample language, unfolded. -/
theorem mem_badLang {p : List Bool} : p ∈ d.badLang ↔ ∀ e : List Bool,
    e.length ≤ d.B * (p.length + 1) ^ d.b → d.Check (pairFstD p) (pairSndD p) e := Iff.rfl

/-- Membership in the inner language, unfolded. -/
theorem mem_innerLang {w : List Bool} :
    w ∈ d.innerLang ↔ ∀ t : List Bool, pairEncode w t ∉ d.badLang := Iff.rfl

/-- Membership in the check language, unfolded. -/
theorem mem_checkLang {q : List Bool} : q ∈ d.checkLang ↔
    d.Check (pairFstD (pairFstD q)) (pairSndD (pairFstD q)) (pairSndD q) := Iff.rfl

/-- The check on a well-formed `w = ⟨x, U⟩`. -/
@[simp] theorem check_pair (x U t e : List Bool) :
    d.Check (pairEncode x U) t e ↔
      t.length ≤ d.B * ((pairEncode x U).length + 1) ^ d.b ∧ d.Core x U t e := by
  simp [Check]

/-- The length of a well-formed instance `⟨⟨x, u⟩, v⟩` is `N(|x|)`. -/
theorem length_inst {x u v : List Bool} (hu : u.length = d.M₁ x)
    (hv : v.length = d.M₂ (pairEncode x u)) :
    (pairEncode (pairEncode x u) v).length = d.nLen x := by
  simp only [length_pairEncode, hv, M₂, hu, nLen, nN, M₁]

end Data

/-! ### The verifier languages -/

/-- A length test against a polynomial of another computed word is in `P`. -/
private theorem lenEq_poly_mem_P {f g : List Bool → List Bool} (hf : PolyTimeComputable f)
    (hg : PolyTimeComputable g) (C c : ℕ) :
    {z | (f z).length = C * ((g z).length + 1) ^ c} ∈ P := by
  have h := lenEq_preimage_mem_P hf (unaryPT_poly C c hg)
  convert h using 1
  ext z
  simp

/-- A length bound by a polynomial of another computed word is in `P`. -/
private theorem lenLe_poly_mem_P {f g : List Bool → List Bool} (hf : PolyTimeComputable f)
    (hg : PolyTimeComputable g) (C c : ℕ) :
    {z | (f z).length ≤ C * ((g z).length + 1) ^ c} ∈ P := by
  have h := lenLe_preimage_mem_P (unaryPT_poly C c hg) hf
  convert h using 1
  ext z
  simp

namespace Data

variable (d : Data)

/-- **The check language is in `P`** (when `R` is).

**Proof sketch.** The check is a Boolean combination of length tests against unary
polynomials, two `CVAL` queries and one `R` query, applied to words computed in polynomial
time from the coordinates (pair projections and re-pairings); `P` is closed under these. -/
theorem checkLang_mem_P (hR : d.R ∈ P) : d.checkLang ∈ P := by
  have hF := polyTimeComputable_pairFstD
  have hS := polyTimeComputable_pairSndD
  have hW : PolyTimeComputable fun q => pairFstD (pairFstD q) := hF.comp hF
  have hT : PolyTimeComputable fun q => pairSndD (pairFstD q) := hS.comp hF
  have hX : PolyTimeComputable fun q => pairFstD (pairFstD (pairFstD q)) := hF.comp hW
  have hU : PolyTimeComputable fun q => pairSndD (pairFstD (pairFstD q)) := hS.comp hW
  have hu : PolyTimeComputable fun q => pairFstD (pairFstD (pairSndD (pairFstD q))) :=
    hF.comp (hF.comp hT)
  have hv' : PolyTimeComputable fun q => pairSndD (pairFstD (pairSndD (pairFstD q))) :=
    hS.comp (hF.comp hT)
  have hw' : PolyTimeComputable fun q => pairFstD (pairSndD (pairSndD (pairFstD q))) :=
    hF.comp (hS.comp hT)
  have hr : PolyTimeComputable fun q => pairSndD (pairSndD (pairSndD (pairFstD q))) :=
    hS.comp (hS.comp hT)
  have hv : PolyTimeComputable fun q => pairFstD (pairSndD q) := hF.comp hS
  have hw : PolyTimeComputable fun q => pairSndD (pairSndD q) := hS.comp hS
  have hy := hX.pairEncode hu
  have hz' := hy.pairEncode hv'
  have hz := hy.pairEncode hv
  exact inter_mem_P (lenLe_poly_mem_P hT hW d.B d.b)
    (inter_mem_P (lenEq_poly_mem_P hu hX d.C₁ d.c₁)
      (union_mem_P
        (inter_mem_P (lenEq_poly_mem_P hv' hy d.C₂ d.c₂)
          (inter_mem_P (preimage_mem_P CVAL_mem_P (hU.pairEncode (hz'.append hw')))
            (inter_mem_P (lenLe_poly_mem_P hr hz' d.C₃ d.c₃)
              (preimage_mem_P hR (hz'.pairEncode hr)))))
        (compl_mem_P (inter_mem_P (lenEq_poly_mem_P hv hy d.C₂ d.c₂)
          (preimage_mem_P CVAL_mem_P (hU.pairEncode (hz.append hw)))))))

/-- **The counterexample language is in `coNP`**: its complement is "some bounded `e`
fails the check", a bounded-certificate `NP` statement over the `P` language `checkLangᶜ`. -/
theorem badLang_mem_coNP (hR : d.R ∈ P) : d.badLang ∈ coNP := by
  show d.badLangᶜ ∈ NP
  refine mem_NP_iff_exists_length_le.mpr ⟨d.B, d.b, d.checkLangᶜ,
    compl_mem_P (d.checkLang_mem_P hR), fun p => ?_⟩
  rw [Set.mem_compl_iff, mem_badLang]
  push_neg
  refine exists_congr fun e => and_congr_right fun _ => ?_
  show _ ↔ ¬ (_ ∈ d.checkLang)
  rw [mem_checkLang, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode]

/-- **The inner language is in `Π₂ᵖ`**: its complement is a bounded `∃` (the check bounds
the universal block) over the `coNP` language `badLang`. -/
theorem innerLang_mem_PiP (hR : d.R ∈ P) : d.innerLang ∈ PiP 2 := by
  show d.innerLangᶜ ∈ SigmaP (1 + 1)
  refine mem_SigmaP_succ_of_exists_le (i := 1) (by rw [PiP_one]; exact d.badLang_mem_coNP hR)
    d.B d.b (fun w t ht hw => hw t ht) (fun w hw => ?_)
  rw [Set.mem_compl_iff, mem_innerLang] at hw
  push_neg at hw
  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := hw
  refine ⟨t, ?_, ht⟩
  have := ((mem_badLang d).mp ht [] (by simp)).1
  simpa using this

end Data

/-! ### Soundness and completeness -/

/-- **Soundness**: if `⟨x, U⟩` is in the inner language, then for every `u` of the right
length, `⟨x, u⟩ ∈ L₂ = ∃·K`. Nothing is assumed about `U`.

**Proof sketch.** The universal block `(u, ε, ε, ε)` must be answered by some `(v, w)`
that matches, since it is no soundness failure: `U` accepts `z = ⟨⟨x, u⟩, v⟩` with
certificate `w`. If `z ∉ K`, a refutation `r` exists, and the universal block
`(u, v, w, r)` is a soundness failure that no answer can defeat. So `z ∈ K`. -/
theorem sound {d : Data} {L₂ K : Language Bool}
    (hL₂ : ∀ y, y ∈ L₂ ↔ ∃ v : List Bool, v.length = d.M₂ y ∧ pairEncode y v ∈ K)
    (hK : ∀ z, z ∈ Kᶜ ↔
      ∃ r : List Bool, r.length ≤ d.C₃ * (z.length + 1) ^ d.c₃ ∧ pairEncode z r ∈ d.R)
    (hB : ∀ x U u v w r : List Bool, u.length = d.M₁ x → v.length ≤ d.M₂ (pairEncode x u) →
      w.length ≤ U.length → r.length ≤ d.C₃ * (d.nLen x + 1) ^ d.c₃ →
      (pairEncode (pairEncode u v) (pairEncode w r)).length ≤
        d.B * ((pairEncode x U).length + 1) ^ d.b)
    {x U : List Bool} (h : pairEncode x U ∈ d.innerLang) (u : List Bool)
    (hu : u.length = d.M₁ x) : pairEncode x u ∈ L₂ := by
  have key : ∀ t : List Bool, t.length ≤ d.B * ((pairEncode x U).length + 1) ^ d.b →
      ∃ e, ¬ d.Core x U t e := by
    intro t ht
    have h' := (d.mem_innerLang.mp h) t
    rw [Data.mem_badLang] at h'
    simp only [pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, Data.check_pair, not_forall] at h'
    obtain ⟨e, -, he⟩ := h'
    exact ⟨e, fun hc => he ⟨ht, hc⟩⟩
  -- the universal block `(u, ε, ε, ε)` is answered by a match
  obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := key (pairEncode (pairEncode u []) (pairEncode [] []))
    (hB x U u [] [] [] hu (by simp) (by simp) (by simp))
  simp only [Data.Core, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, hu, true_and, not_or,
    not_not] at he
  obtain ⟨-, hv, hq⟩ := he
  refine (hL₂ _).mpr ⟨pairFstD e, hv, ?_⟩
  -- the matched instance is in `K`: otherwise its refutation is a soundness failure
  by_contra hz
  obtain ⟨r, hr, hR⟩ := (hK _).mp hz
  have hzl := d.length_inst hu hv
  have hwl : (pairSndD e).length ≤ U.length :=
    le_trans (by simp) (length_le_of_query hq)
  obtain ⟨e₁, he₁⟩ := key (pairEncode (pairEncode u (pairFstD e)) (pairEncode (pairSndD e) r))
    (hB x U u _ _ r hu hv.le hwl (hzl ▸ hr))
  simp only [Data.Core, pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, hu, true_and, not_or] at he₁
  exact he₁.1 ⟨hv, hq, hr, hR⟩

/-- **Completeness**: if `D` decides `K` as nondeterministic circuits and `x ∈ L`, then
`⟨x, ⌜D_{N(|x|)}⌝⟩` is in the inner language.

**Proof sketch.** Take a universal block `t` with `|u|` right (otherwise the check fails
outright). Since `⟨x, u⟩ ∈ ∃·K` there is `v` with `z = ⟨⟨x, u⟩, v⟩ ∈ K`, and a certificate
`y` with `D_{|z|}(z, y) = 1`; `|z| = N(|x|)`, so `e = ⟨v, y⟩` is a match. And `t` is no
soundness failure: an instance accepted by `D_{N(|x|)}` is in `K`, so it has no refutation. -/
theorem complete {d : Data} {L₂ K : Language Bool}
    (hL₂ : ∀ y, y ∈ L₂ ↔ ∃ v : List Bool, v.length = d.M₂ y ∧ pairEncode y v ∈ K)
    (hK : ∀ z, z ∈ Kᶜ ↔
      ∃ r : List Bool, r.length ≤ d.C₃ * (z.length + 1) ^ d.c₃ ∧ pairEncode z r ∈ d.R)
    {m : ℕ → ℕ} {D : (n : ℕ) → DAGCircuit (n + m n)} (hD : ∀ n, (D n).IsFaninTwo)
    (hKD : ∀ z : List Bool, z ∈ K ↔
      ∃ y : Fin (m z.length) → Bool, (D z.length).eval (Fin.append z.get y) = true)
    (hB : ∀ x U t v w : List Bool,
      v.length ≤ d.C₂ * (2 * x.length + 2 + d.M₁ x + 1) ^ d.c₂ → w.length ≤ U.length →
      (pairEncode v w).length ≤ d.B * ((pairEncode (pairEncode x U) t).length + 1) ^ d.b)
    {x : List Bool} (hx : ∀ u : List Bool, u.length = d.M₁ x → pairEncode x u ∈ L₂) :
    pairEncode x (D (d.nLen x)).encode ∈ d.innerLang := by
  rw [Data.mem_innerLang]
  intro t ht
  rw [Data.mem_badLang] at ht
  simp only [pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, Data.check_pair] at ht
  set U := (D (d.nLen x)).encode with hU
  set u := pairFstD (pairFstD t) with hu_def
  -- an instance of length `N(|x|)` accepted by `U` is in `K`
  have hqK : ∀ z w : List Bool, z.length = d.nLen x → Query U (z ++ w) → z ∈ K := by
    intro z w hz hq
    obtain ⟨y, -, hev⟩ := (query_append_iff D hD z w hz).mp hq
    exact (hKD z).mpr ⟨y, hev⟩
  by_cases hu : u.length = d.M₁ x
  · obtain ⟨v, hv, hz⟩ := (hL₂ _).mp (hx u hu)
    have hzl := d.length_inst hu hv
    obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := (hKD _).mp hz
    have hm : (List.ofFn y).length ≤ U.length := by
      have hs := (D (pairEncode (pairEncode x u) v).length).size_le_length_encode
      simp only [DAGCircuit.size] at hs
      rw [List.length_ofFn, hU]
      rw [hzl] at hs ⊢
      omega
    have hvl : v.length ≤ d.C₂ * (2 * x.length + 2 + d.M₁ x + 1) ^ d.c₂ := by
      rw [hv, Data.M₂, length_pairEncode, hu]
    obtain ⟨-, -, hsf | hnm⟩ := ht (pairEncode v (List.ofFn y)) (hB x U t v _ hvl hm)
    · obtain ⟨hv', hq', hr', hR'⟩ := hsf
      exact (hK _).mpr ⟨_, hr', hR'⟩ (hqK _ _ (d.length_inst hu hv') hq')
    · simp only [pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode] at hnm
      exact hnm ⟨hv, (query_append_iff D hD _ _ hzl).mpr ⟨y, rfl, hy⟩⟩
  · exact hu (ht [] (by simp)).2.1

/-! ### Polynomial bounds -/

/-- Sums of polynomially bounded functions are polynomially bounded. -/
private theorem polyBound_add {f g : ℕ → ℕ} (hf : PolyBound f) (hg : PolyBound g) :
    PolyBound fun n => f n + g n := by
  obtain ⟨A, α, hA⟩ := hf
  obtain ⟨B, β, hB⟩ := hg
  refine ⟨A + B, α + β, fun n => ?_⟩
  have h1 : (n + 1) ^ α ≤ (n + 1) ^ (α + β) := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega) (by omega)
  have h2 : (n + 1) ^ β ≤ (n + 1) ^ (α + β) := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega) (by omega)
  have := hA n
  have := hB n
  nlinarith

/-- A polynomial of a polynomially bounded function is polynomially bounded. -/
private theorem polyBound_comp {f : ℕ → ℕ} (hf : PolyBound f) (C c : ℕ) :
    PolyBound fun n => C * (f n + 1) ^ c := by
  obtain ⟨A, α, hA⟩ := hf
  refine ⟨C * (A + 1) ^ c, α * c, fun n => ?_⟩
  have hone : 1 ≤ (n + 1) ^ α := Nat.one_le_pow _ _ (by omega)
  have h1 : f n + 1 ≤ (A + 1) * (n + 1) ^ α := by have := hA n; nlinarith
  calc C * (f n + 1) ^ c ≤ C * ((A + 1) * (n + 1) ^ α) ^ c :=
        Nat.mul_le_mul_left C (Nat.pow_le_pow_left h1 c)
    _ = C * (A + 1) ^ c * (n + 1) ^ (α * c) := by rw [mul_pow, ← pow_mul, mul_assoc]

/-- A constant multiple of a polynomially bounded function is polynomially bounded. -/
private theorem polyBound_smul (q : ℕ) {f : ℕ → ℕ} (hf : PolyBound f) :
    PolyBound fun n => q * f n := by
  obtain ⟨A, α, hA⟩ := hf
  exact ⟨q * A, α, fun n => by rw [mul_assoc]; exact Nat.mul_le_mul_left q (hA n)⟩

/-- `A (n+1)^α + 2s ≤ (A+2) W^{α+1}` when `n + 1 ≤ W` and `s ≤ W`. -/
private theorem bound_aux {A α n W s : ℕ} (hn : n + 1 ≤ W) (hs : s ≤ W) :
    A * (n + 1) ^ α + 2 * s ≤ (A + 2) * W ^ (α + 1) := by
  have hW : 1 ≤ W := by omega
  have h1 : (n + 1) ^ α ≤ W ^ (α + 1) :=
    (Nat.pow_le_pow_left hn α).trans (Nat.pow_le_pow_right hW (by omega))
  have h2 : W ≤ W ^ (α + 1) := by
    calc W = W ^ 1 := (pow_one W).symm
      _ ≤ W ^ (α + 1) := Nat.pow_le_pow_right hW (by omega)
  nlinarith

end Complexity.Yap

namespace Complexity

open Turing BoolCircuit Yap

/-- **`Π₃ᵖ ⊆ Σ₃ᵖ` under `coNP ⊆ NP/poly`** (the core of [Yap83, Theorem 2]).

**Proof sketch.** Write `x ∈ L ⟺ ∀ u ∃ v, ⟨⟨x, u⟩, v⟩ ∈ K` with `K ∈ coNP` and
`z ∈ Kᶜ ⟺ ∃ r, ⟨z, r⟩ ∈ R`, and let `D` be `NP/poly` circuits for `K`. Then
`x ∈ L ⟺ ∃ U (|U| ≤ poly), ⟨x, U⟩ ∈ innerLang` with `innerLang ∈ Π₂ᵖ`: (⇐) by `sound`,
(⇒) with `U` the description of `D_{N(|x|)}` by `complete`. All lengths involved are
bounded by one polynomial `A (|x|+1)^α`, which fixes the bound constants of the checks. -/
theorem PiP_three_subset_SigmaP_three_of_coNP_subset_NPPoly
    (h : coNP ⊆ {L | L.InNPPoly}) : PiP 3 ⊆ SigmaP 3 := by
  intro L hL
  obtain ⟨C₁, c₁, L₂, hL₂S, hLx⟩ := mem_PiP_succ_iff.mp (show L ∈ PiP (2 + 1) from hL)
  obtain ⟨C₂, c₂, K, hKco, hL₂x⟩ := mem_SigmaP_two_iff.mp hL₂S
  obtain ⟨C₃, c₃, R, hR, hKc⟩ := mem_NP_iff_exists_length_le.mp (show Kᶜ ∈ NP from hKco)
  obtain ⟨a, k, m, D, hD, hDs, hKD⟩ := h hKco
  -- one polynomial bounding every length of the construction
  obtain ⟨A, α, hA⟩ : PolyBound fun n => 4 * (C₁ * (n + 1) ^ c₁) +
      2 * (C₂ * (2 * n + 2 + C₁ * (n + 1) ^ c₁ + 1) ^ c₂) + 8 +
      C₃ * (nN C₁ c₁ C₂ c₂ n + 1) ^ c₃ + 12 * (a * (nN C₁ c₁ C₂ c₂ n + 1) ^ k) ^ 2 := by
    have hP1 : PolyBound fun n => C₁ * (n + 1) ^ c₁ := ⟨C₁, c₁, fun _ => le_rfl⟩
    have hY : PolyBound fun n => 2 * n + 2 + C₁ * (n + 1) ^ c₁ :=
      polyBound_add ⟨4, 1, fun n => by nlinarith⟩ hP1
    have hM2 := polyBound_comp hY C₂ c₂
    have hN : PolyBound fun n => nN C₁ c₁ C₂ c₂ n :=
      polyBound_add (polyBound_add (polyBound_smul 2 hY) ⟨2, 0, fun n => by simp⟩) hM2
    have hsq : PolyBound fun n => (a * (nN C₁ c₁ C₂ c₂ n + 1) ^ k) ^ 2 := by
      obtain ⟨B, β, hB⟩ := polyBound_comp (polyBound_comp hN a k) 1 2
      refine ⟨B, β, fun n => (Nat.pow_le_pow_left (Nat.le_succ _) 2).trans ?_⟩
      simpa only [one_mul] using hB n
    exact polyBound_add (polyBound_add (polyBound_add (polyBound_add (polyBound_smul 4 hP1)
      (polyBound_smul 2 hM2)) ⟨8, 0, fun n => by simp⟩) (polyBound_comp hN C₃ c₃))
      (polyBound_smul 12 hsq)
  let d : Data := ⟨C₁, c₁, C₂, c₂, C₃, c₃, A + 2, α + 1, R⟩
  have hBs : ∀ x U u v w r : List Bool, u.length = d.M₁ x → v.length ≤ d.M₂ (pairEncode x u) →
      w.length ≤ U.length → r.length ≤ d.C₃ * (d.nLen x + 1) ^ d.c₃ →
      (pairEncode (pairEncode u v) (pairEncode w r)).length ≤
        d.B * ((pairEncode x U).length + 1) ^ d.b := by
    intro x U u v w r hu hv hw hr
    have hE := hA x.length
    simp only [Data.M₁, Data.M₂, Data.nLen, length_pairEncode] at hu hv hr ⊢
    rw [hu] at hv
    have hb := bound_aux (A := A) (α := α) (n := x.length)
      (W := 2 * x.length + 2 + U.length + 1) (s := U.length) (by omega) (by omega)
    show _ ≤ (A + 2) * _
    nlinarith
  have hBc : ∀ x U t v w : List Bool,
      v.length ≤ d.C₂ * (2 * x.length + 2 + d.M₁ x + 1) ^ d.c₂ → w.length ≤ U.length →
      (pairEncode v w).length ≤ d.B * ((pairEncode (pairEncode x U) t).length + 1) ^ d.b := by
    intro x U t v w hv hw
    have hE := hA x.length
    beta_reduce at hE
    simp only [d, Data.M₁, length_pairEncode] at hv ⊢
    have hb := bound_aux (A := A) (α := α) (n := x.length)
      (W := 2 * (2 * x.length + 2 + U.length) + 2 + t.length + 1) (s := U.length)
      (by omega) (by omega)
    omega
  refine Yap.mem_SigmaP_succ_of_exists_le (i := 2) (d.innerLang_mem_PiP hR) A α
    (fun x U hU => (hLx x).mpr fun u hu => sound hL₂x hKc hBs hU u hu) (fun x hx => ?_)
  refine ⟨(D (d.nLen x)).encode, ?_, complete hL₂x hKc hD hKD hBc ((hLx x).mp hx)⟩
  have henc := (D (d.nLen x)).length_encode_le_of_isFaninTwo (hD _)
  have hsz := Nat.pow_le_pow_left (hDs (d.nLen x)) 2
  have hE := hA x.length
  beta_reduce at hE
  simp only [d, Data.nLen] at henc hsz ⊢
  omega

/-- **Yap's theorem** [Yap83, Theorem 2]: if `coNP ⊆ NP/poly` then `PH = Σ₃ᵖ`.

**Proof sketch.** `Π₃ᵖ ⊆ Σ₃ᵖ` (`PiP_three_subset_SigmaP_three_of_coNP_subset_NPPoly`) and
the collapse [AB09, Theorem 5.4] (`PH_eq_SigmaP_of_PiP_subset_SigmaP`). -/
theorem PH_eq_SigmaP_three_of_coNP_subset_NPPoly (h : coNP ⊆ {L | L.InNPPoly}) :
    PH = SigmaP 3 :=
  PH_eq_SigmaP_of_PiP_subset_SigmaP (by norm_num)
    (PiP_three_subset_SigmaP_three_of_coNP_subset_NPPoly h)

end Complexity

namespace Randomized

open Complexity

/-- **[AB09, Exercise 7.8]**: if `3SATᶜ ∈ BP·NP` then `PH = Σ₃ᵖ`.

**Proof sketch.** `coNP ⊆ NP/poly` (`coNP_subset_NPPoly_of_compl_SAT3_mem_BPNP`, via
[AB09, Exercise 7.7]) and Yap's theorem (`PH_eq_SigmaP_three_of_coNP_subset_NPPoly`). -/
theorem PH_eq_SigmaP_three_of_compl_SAT3_mem_BPNP (h : SAT3ᶜ ∈ BPNP) : PH = SigmaP 3 :=
  PH_eq_SigmaP_three_of_coNP_subset_NPPoly (coNP_subset_NPPoly_of_compl_SAT3_mem_BPNP h)

end Randomized
